title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 1.6 Attributes of God

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

An attribute is a quality that shows what someone is like. In this sub-strand you will read 1 John 4:7-8, Genesis 1:1-25 and 1 Samuel 2:2, and name God as Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father. You will learn that this loving Father knows you by your name.

## Strand 1.0: Creation
Sub-strand 1.6: Attributes of God
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) read scriptures on the attributes of God
b) list three attributes of God and revere Him
c) recognise God as a loving Father who knows them by their names

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you know the attributes of God?

## Core competencies
• Collaboration: the skill of teamwork is portrayed as they sort and match letters.
• Creativity and Imagination: the skill of exploration is exhibited as learners compose a poem on, ‘God our loving Father.’

## Values
• Unity is nurtured as they work in groups and sing a song about the love of God.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social cohesion: is portrayed as learners interact with each other while working in groups to picture-read the Bible texts.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: writing skills are applied as learners write a poem.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are reinforced as learners sing a song about the love of God.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 1.0 Creation, Sub-strand 1.6 Attributes of God
• Genesis 1:1-25; 1 John 4:7-8; 1 Samuel 2:2

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Three attributes of God

LESSON 1: THREE ATTRIBUTES OF GOD
=================================

## What you will learn
• Read scriptures on the attributes of God.
• List three attributes of God: Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father.
• Show reverence for God.

Curriculum outcomes: a) read scriptures on the attributes of God; b) list three attributes of God and revere Him

## Introduction
You can describe a friend as kind or brave. Those words are qualities. The Bible also gives qualities of God. They are called His attributes. Knowing them helps you worship Him as He truly is.

## Notes
An attribute of God is something that is always true about Him. People can change. God does not stop being who He is. In this sub-strand we learn three attributes: Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father.

### Sole Creator: Genesis 1:1-25
Genesis 1:1 says that in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. Verses 1 to 25 tell how He made light, the sky, the dry land and the seas, plants, the sun, the moon and the stars, fish and birds, and the animals on the land. He did this by His word. No other god made the world. Sole Creator means He alone is the Maker. When you see a river, a tree or the night sky, you are looking at His work.

### Loving Father: 1 John 4:7-8
1 John 4:7-8 tells believers to love one another, because love comes from God. The passage says that God is love. A person who does not love does not know God. Love is not a mood God sometimes has. Love is what He is. He is a Father who loves.

### Holy Father: 1 Samuel 2:2
In 1 Samuel 2:2 Hannah prays, "There is no one holy like the LORD." Holy means pure, set apart, and completely good. There is no evil in God. He is also called a Rock, strong and safe. Because He is holy, we revere Him. Revere means to honour Him with deep respect, in the way we speak, pray and obey.

### Sorting the words
You can sort letters and join words from a puzzle: sole creator, loving, holy. Say them aloud. These three attributes belong together. The Creator is not far away and uncaring. He is the holy God, and He is love.

## Key words
• attribute — a quality that shows what someone is like
• sole — the only one; no other
• holy — pure, set apart, and completely good
• revere — to honour with deep respect

## Activity: Picture-read the three passages
You will need: Bible, Letter cards, Word puzzle
1. In groups, picture-read 1 John 4:7-8, Genesis 1:1-25 and 1 Samuel 2:2 in turns.
2. Sort and match letters to spell Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father.
3. Join the words sole creator, loving and holy from a puzzle.
4. Each group tells the class which verse matches which attribute.

## Practice
1. What is an attribute of God?
2. Which passage shows that God is the Sole Creator?
3. List the three attributes of God in this sub-strand.
4. Which verse says there is no one holy like the LORD?

## Summary
• Genesis 1:1-25 shows God as the Sole Creator.
• 1 John 4:7-8 says God is love.
• 1 Samuel 2:2 says there is no one holy like the LORD.

### Answers to practice
1. A quality that is true about God, such as holy or loving.
2. Genesis 1:1-25.
3. Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father.
4. 1 Samuel 2:2.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: God our loving Father knows our names

LESSON 2: GOD OUR LOVING FATHER KNOWS OUR NAMES
===============================================

## What you will learn
• Recognise God as a loving Father who knows each learner by name.
• Compose a short poem on "God our loving Father."

Curriculum outcomes: c) recognise God as a loving Father who knows them by their names

## Introduction
A good father knows the names of his children. He does not call them "that one" and walk past. The Bible teaches that God is a Father like that, only greater, because He is holy and He is love.

## Notes
A loving father provides, protects, corrects and listens. God does all of this perfectly. He is not loving one day and cruel the next. 1 John 4:8 says God is love, so His care does not run out.

### He knows you by name
You learnt to say your own name so that people can identify you. God already knows that name. He knew you when He formed you. When Jesus called Zacchaeus, He used his name. The same God knows your name in this class. You are not hidden in a crowd. You can pray, "Father, You know me," and you are telling the truth.

Knowing your name also means He knows your joys and your troubles. You can tell Him when you are afraid. A loving Father wants His children to speak to Him.

### How we respond
- Call Him Father when you pray.
- Obey Him because you love Him, not only because you fear punishment.
- Love other people, since love comes from God.
- Revere Him. Do not use His name as a joke.
- Thank Him for creating you and for daily care.

### A poem and a song
Compose a short poem that begins, "God our loving Father." You might write about Him making the world, loving you, and knowing your name. Read it to the group. Then sing a song about the love of God. Working and singing together builds unity.

Why should you know God's attributes? Because you worship what you know. If you know He is the only Creator, you will not trust another god. If you know He is holy, you will hate sin. If you know He is a loving Father, you will come to Him with your real name and your real needs.

## Key words
• loving Father — God, who cares for His children perfectly because He is love
• revere — to honour God with deep respect

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner says, "God is too busy to know a child in Grade 4." How do the attributes of God answer her?

Working:
1. God is the Sole Creator, so the whole world is His work, including her.
2. God is love, so He is not too busy to care.
3. As a loving Father He knows His children by name.

Answer: God is not too busy. He is the Creator and a loving Father who knows her by name.

## Activity: Poem: God our loving Father
You will need: Exercise book, Pencil
1. In groups, talk about how a loving father treats his children, and how God is greater.
2. Each learner composes a short poem on "God our loving Father," including the idea that He knows us by name.
3. Read the poems aloud.
4. Sing a song about the love of God.

## Practice
1. What does it mean that God knows you by your name?
2. Which attribute tells us that God's care does not run out?
3. Give one way to respond to God as a loving Father.

## Summary
• God is a loving Father, and love is what He is.
• He knows each child by name.
• We respond by praying, obeying, loving others and revering Him.

### Answers to practice
1. He knows who I am personally and cares for me as His child. I am not lost in a crowd.
2. Loving Father, because God is love.
3. Any one: pray to Him as Father, obey Him, love other people, revere His name, thank Him.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 1.6 ATTRIBUTES OF GOD
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. An attribute of God is...
   A. a story we invent about Him
   B. a quality that is true about Him
   C. the name of a classmate
   D. a book of the Bible

2. Which passage do we read to see God as Sole Creator?
   A. Genesis 1:1-25
   B. Ephesians 6:1-3
   C. Luke 19:2-10
   D. Matthew 5:42

3. 1 John 4:8 says that God is...
   A. fear
   B. love
   C. a man like us
   D. far away and uncaring

4. "There is no one holy like the LORD" comes from...
   A. 1 Samuel 2:2
   B. Genesis 12:3
   C. Luke 1:37
   D. Psalm 139:13

5. Which three attributes belong to this sub-strand?

6. Sole Creator means...
   A. God made the world together with many gods
   B. God alone made the heavens and the earth
   C. people made themselves
   D. only plants were created

7. To revere God means...
   A. to ignore Him
   B. to honour Him with deep respect
   C. to use His name as a joke
   D. to fear Him and run away forever

8. How is God a loving Father to you?

9. A learner says God is too busy to know her name. The best answer is...
   A. She is right because Grade 4 is small
   B. God knows her by name because He is a loving Father
   C. Only adults are known by God
   D. Names do not matter to the Creator

10. Why should you know the attributes of God?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 1.6 ATTRIBUTES OF GOD
========================================

1. B. a quality that is true about Him
   Attributes are God's qualities, such as holy and loving.

2. A. Genesis 1:1-25
   Genesis 1:1-25 tells how God alone made the world.

3. B. love
   The verse says God is love.

4. A. 1 Samuel 2:2
   Hannah's prayer in 1 Samuel 2:2 speaks of God's holiness.

5. Sole Creator, Loving Father and Holy Father.
   These are the three attributes learners sort, match and puzzle out.

6. B. God alone made the heavens and the earth
   Sole means the only one. Genesis 1 shows God creating by His word.

7. B. to honour Him with deep respect
   Reverence is deep respect shown in worship and obedience.

8. He cares, provides, protects and knows me by my name.
   A loving father knows his children. God does this perfectly.

9. B. God knows her by name because He is a loving Father
   God the loving Father knows each person personally.

10. So that you worship Him as He truly is: the only Creator, holy, and love.
   Knowing who God is guides reverence and trust.
